static_traits.name: Tang Sikai
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive friends and family, but finds it hard to share with them when facing specific work problems; relationships with colleagues are affected by worrying about not being trusted.
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychological counseling; in the past, similar feelings of failure and self-doubt occurred under work stress or when making mistakes.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic, somewhat negative tone; often uses absolute and catastrophic expressions (such as 'will never be trusted again'); good cooperation.

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I disappointed a student today and worry this mistake means I will never be trusted again. This feeling of failure and not being trusted began with a specific recent incident at work and keeps ruminating, affecting my work performance and sleep.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of failure and worries about not being trusted are affecting my work performance and causing significant distress.
growth_experiences: In the past, work-related stress or mistakes often triggered strong feelings of failure and self-doubt, and he tended to cope through repeated rumination, but found it hard to relieve; he had not received psychological counseling before.
Family of origin background: the youngest of four siblings.

core_beliefs: Only by being perfect is one worth trusting
Once I make a mistake, others will no longer trust me

special_situations.event: Provided inappropriate/incorrect advice to a student at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake, I will permanently lose others' trust in me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Eagerly seeks comfort and reassurance from colleagues to relieve unease
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have disappointed my students; I will never be trusted again

special_situations.event: After receiving negative feedback in professional settings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative feedback means I am incompetent; it shows I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly replays events and ruminates over details to find 'a better answer' and try to make amends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves I am incompetent; everyone will think I am unreliable

special_situations.event: When discussing events with colleagues or anticipating interactions with colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not perfect, they will think I am not trustworthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeking external recognition and comfort, or avoiding sharing specific details with family and friends

special_situations.event: Alone at night, preparing to sleep, recalling work mistakes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only continuous reflection and maintaining high vigilance can avoid worse consequences
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to maintain control and prevent recurrence through continuous rumination
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: From now on, everything will go downhill

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be trusted, recognized as a reliable and capable professional
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as incompetent, being rejected, and losing credibility (not being trusted)
defense_goal: Avoiding failure and others' distrust through self-reproach and pursuit of perfection
Relieving anxiety and maintaining a sense of security by seeking reassurance from others
Staying cautious, reducing exposure of vulnerability to avoid negative evaluation

object_relations.self_representation: Easily being defined by mistakes as a failure, fragile and untrusted person
object_relations.object_representation: Picky colleagues or students who may withdraw trust and pass judgment

object_relations.self_representation: A professional helper who can be seen and trusted when supported by others
object_relations.object_representation: Colleagues and students who can understand and support

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks 'is there evidence supporting that no one trusts you anymore' or proposes reality testing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiences the counselor's exploration as questioning and potential judgment, worrying that incompetence will be exposed and they will be rejected
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Highlights imaginings of the worst scenario, with a heavy tone, continues to emphasize the worry of 'ruining one's reputation', and for now does not acknowledge positive evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about interactions with colleagues or students and anticipating others' reactions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes others will view them as incompetent (transference: projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses speculative language (such as 'they will...'), focuses on others' views rather than their own feelings, with a cautious tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing the internal standard 'I must be perfect to be trusted'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Uncritically internalizing harsh external evaluations and rules as self-demands
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Frequently uses 'should / must' sentence patterns, emphasizing rules and standards, with a harsh and self-restricting tone.

manifestations: Worries that because of one mistake, colleagues and students will no longer trust them and relationships may become estranged
Finds it hard to share specific work problems with relatives and friends, feeling isolated in the career predicament
Bound by inner high expectations and the condition of worth 'must be perfect to be worthy of trust'
Difficulty with self-acceptance and flexible choices when facing mistakes

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses expressions of 'I must / should...' (such as 'I need to be perfect to be worthy of trust' and 'I should have known better')
Taking external evaluations unconditionally as one's self-standard

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly ruminating on mistakes, emphasizing 'must not make mistakes'
Caring excessively about others' evaluations, worrying about losing trust
Excessively cautious when expressing needs and sharing problems

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Speculates that colleagues and students will think they are incompetent ('they will no longer trust me')
Attributes inner self-doubt to others' negative views

exception_events.target_problem: When making mistakes or under pressure at work, the client usually falls into worries about failure and not being trusted, ruminates and seeks reassurance from others, leading to decreased work performance and disturbed sleep.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During a crisis intervention last semester, the client effectively supported a student; the student expressed gratitude and gave positive feedback, and he experienced being trusted and a sense of competence.
exception_events.reason: Clue: On that occasion he was present in time and provided effective support, receiving direct and clear positive feedback, so in that moment the experience of self-efficacy and being trusted was more prominent.

positive_force: Multiple past experiences of successfully helping others and positive feedback
Willing to seek counseling and try reality testing and cognitive balance
Able to recall specific success cases, with reflection and self-awareness
negative_force: Self-blame caused by perfectionism and high self-expectations
Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and mind reading
High dependence on external recognition (seeking reassurance)
Rumination worsens anxiety and insomnia, reducing work efficiency

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly ruminates on work-related mistakes and engages in self-deprecation
antecedent: 在专业环境中发生失误
Receiving negative feedback or recalling related events
target_behavior.core_reason: Inner high expectations and fear of disappointing others, accompanied by catastrophizing and all-or-nothing thinking to maintain a sense of control over mistakes
target_behavior.function: Attempts through rumination to gain control, prevent recurrence, and self-punish to conform to internalized standards
target_behavior.consequence: Disturbed sleep, increased anxiety, decreased work efficiency, strained relationships with colleagues

target_behavior.behavior: Frequently seeking comfort and reassurance from colleagues
antecedent: After making mistakes, feels distrusted or anticipates negative evaluations from others
target_behavior.core_reason: Reliance on external approval to relieve self-doubt and anxiety
target_behavior.function: Gains comfort and security in the short term, attempting to confirm own worth and the reliability of own judgment
target_behavior.consequence: Dependence on external evaluation increases, making it hard to form a stable self-evaluation, and interpersonal relationships remain strained
